summary.goal: Define core domain entities for the Forge execution engine: Run, Task, TaskAttempt, Artifact, and their state machines. These types form the foundation for all Forge operations.

acceptance_criteria.description: Run entity with states: pending, running, paused, completed, failed, cancelled
Task entity with states: pending, queued, running, auditing, awaiting_approval, completed, failed, blocked
TaskAttempt tracks individual execution attempts with start/end times and outcome
Artifact type represents references to produced work (commit, PR, file, deployment)
State transitions are validated - invalid transitions throw errors
ForgePlan and ForgeStep types define the contract with Planner
Run entity includes has_pending_gate flag for gate-based scheduling pause

observations: Run is the top-level execution unit, contains multiple Tasks
Task maps 1:1 to a ForgeStep from the plan
TaskAttempt enables retry tracking - multiple attempts per task
Artifacts are references, not content - live in their natural homes
State machines must be explicit and validated
awaiting_approval state used when human gate is reached
has_pending_gate flag pauses task scheduling while gate is pending
patterns: State machine pattern for Run and Task lifecycle
Reference-based artifacts (commit SHA, PR URL, file path)

steps.title: Create state transition validators

acceptance_criteria.description: VALID_RUN_TRANSITIONS map: { pending: ['running'], running: ['paused', 'completed', 'failed', 'cancelled'], paused: ['running', 'cancelled'], ... }

transitionRun(run, newStatus) returns updated Run with validated transition

architecture.pattern: State machine with explicit transition map
architecture.validation: Throw descriptive error on invalid transition
